source.title: Beyond Language: Format-Agnostic Reasoning Subspaces in Large Language Models

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests representational convergence with RSA, CKA, cross-form patching, and subspace interventions rather than reproducing the original cross-modal measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own measurements of representational geometry and cross-form transfer, which bear on the claim. Results it cites from prior work are not recorded. The row limit requires leaving out some reported probes, ablation results, and control results.
record.test_reason: Only §4.5 (Table 10, Fig. 9) compares representations across independently trained models. It reports CCA between per-model 10-dim FARS subspaces for five base LLMs from three families, a different method aimed at the V1 question. All other results (concept/form RSA, dimension-wise CKA, cross-form patching, subspace patching) measure alignment between input formats inside a single model. That is a different construct from cross-model convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a low-dimensional format-agnostic reasoning subspace exists in middle layers and is causally sufficient for cross-form patching. They also conclude it converges across architectures (CCA > 0.79), which they frame as within-modality evidence for the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. They qualify this with a declarative-procedural asymmetry and with global form dominance.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines symbolic-form invariance within text models, using permutation-corrected RSA, CKA, cross-form probing, and activation interventions rather than testing vision-language alignment across modalities.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with the form pair: EN→Math patching is consistently much higher than EN→Code patching. The paper also reports layer-dependent patching, strongest at early-to-middle layers and weaker toward later layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Within single models, concept structure is weak globally (concept RSA 0.10–0.20) and dominated by surface form (form RSA 0.43–0.53). Cross-format CKA is 0.73–0.87. Prose→math patching preserves far more than prose→code (0.65–0.73 vs 0.16–0.22). A 10-dim concept-centroid subspace preserves 90–96% of output under cross-form patching, vs 44–56% for full replacement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a language model, the same content expressed in different symbolic formats shares a low-dimensional, causally used subspace. The sharing is much weaker between declarative and procedural (code) formats.

record.problems: The largest model is 8B; only base models and programmatically generated stimuli are tested. The paper does not measure model capability or use a controlled scale sweep. The reported 95% confidence intervals for FARS overlap in Table 5 do not contain the corresponding point values. The study also notes that structural invariance has only one structured-data form.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted results include cross-form probe accuracies (Tables 1 and 4), subspace-ablation KL values and random-direction controls (Table 5), and pairwise centroid RSA values (Table 10). These were omitted after retaining per-model scale and dimension measurements, form-pair differences, FARS/PCA/full-patching results, and cross-model CCA comparisons.

untested.parts: Capability is not measured. Models stop at 8B. There is no controlled scale sweep. Cross-model alignment is measured only inside a supervised, label-selected 10-dim subspace, not in full representations, and there is no null baseline.
No vision models or image-caption pairs.
No cross-model mapping, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment. CCA shows linear relatedness of the subspaces but no transfer between models.
No neuron, SAE-feature or circuit matching across models.
Cross-model alignment is reported only with CCA and centroid RSA on one stimulus set. Measure settings, input distribution and full-space vs subspace are not varied across models.
Whether shared data or objectives cause the cross-model alignment, and whether it plateaus, are not tested. Same-family vs cross-family differences are small and uncontrolled.

record.verdict_notes: Most rows measure within-model format invariance, not cross-model convergence. The reader's V1 scale labels on concept RSA and CKA, the V4 label on within-model patching, and the V6/V7 labels are reassigned to none. Cross-model convergence rests only on Table 10. That alignment is computed inside a subspace each model gets from concept labels at its best layer, with no random or null CCA baseline, so high CCA may partly reflect the shared 18-concept labelling. Centroid RSA in Fig. 9 conflicts with Table 10 (e.g. GPT-2 vs Qwen-3B 0.84 vs 0.79; Qwen-3B vs Llama 0.91 vs 0.82). The Table 5 CIs exclude their point estimates. Base models only, at most 8B, synthetic stimuli, preprint.

versions.untested_parts: It compares different model sizes and reports alignment measures, but does not measure capability or conduct a controlled scale sweep holding architecture, data, and objective fixed.
No vision models or paired image-caption representations are tested.
No same-architecture comparisons across random initializations, shared features, or shared subspaces across seeds are reported.
Tests cross-form activation and subspace patching, not stitching layers, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
It extracts a concept subspace but does not test whether the same interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits recur across models.
It compares several symbolic-form pairs and several geometry measures, but does not systematically vary similarity-measure settings such as neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.
The paper reports incomplete alignment and form dominance, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause the alignment, or whether it plateaus over a controlled scale sweep.

rows.note: FARS was extracted at each model's best layer.
rows.check: Cross-family CCA of 0.79–0.90 on per-model FARS subspaces at each model's best layer. Pairs that include the smallest model (GPT-2 XL) are lowest (0.79–0.83); pairs among 7–8B models are highest (0.86–0.90). Caveats: the subspace is supervised, chosen with concept labels and best layer, and no null or random-model CCA baseline is given.

relationships.condition: Cross-model CCA on per-model 10-dim FARS subspaces (best layer), five base LLMs 1.6B–8B across GPT, Qwen and Llama/Mistral families, TriForm stimuli
relationships.reason: All cross-family pairs reach CCA 0.79–0.90. GPT-2 XL pairs are lowest (0.79–0.83) and 7–8B pairs highest (0.86–0.90), consistent with stronger alignment among larger models (r51–r60).
relationships.display_finding: Cross-family CCA ranged from 0.79 to 0.90, with GPT-2 XL pairs lowest at 0.79–0.83 and 7–8B pairs highest at 0.86–0.90.
